newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker amid supply concerns.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker amid supply concerns.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Tuesday, although spreads to U.S. long bonds narrowed as the pressure of new and upcoming Canadian and U.S. supply weighed on prices in both countries, analysts said.

"We've had auctions in the U.S. and we have a 10-year auction in Canada tomorrow, so I think it's more a slight retracement or a slight concession to supply than anything," said Barry Allan, vice-president of global fixed income with Altamira Investment Services Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.28 to C$111.10 to yield 7.06 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 4/32 to yield 6.89 percent. The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 17 basis points from 18 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.

The U.S. Treasury on Tuesday auctioned US$17 billion of three year notes as part of its quarterly refunding, and on Wednesday will auction US$12 billion in 10-year notes. While the three-year auction produced the expected yield, demand for the auction was described as soggy and weighed on bond prices.
Investors are now looking ahead to 10-year auctions on both sides of the border.
The Canadian government on Wednesday will auction C$2.4 billion of bonds with a coupon of 7.25 percent and maturing on June 1, 2007. Results of the auction will be released at 1315/1715.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bonds fell C$0.15 to C$103.45 to yield 6.508 percent. The U.S. bond fell 5/32 to yield 6.67 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 16 basis points from 18 basis points on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.02 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.18 percent.
